headers.comment: Security headers on everything the site itself serves. The source excludes /__/ — Firebase's own reserved pages, which include the Google sign-in popup and iframe — so a policy written for this app can never be applied to pages it does not control. script-src is the part that matters: only this site's own files and Google's sign-in loader may run as code, so text that reaches the page from the AI, from OpenStreetMap or from another member of a trip cannot become a script. frame-ancestors lists the site's own four addresses because the sign-in iframe lives on the .firebaseapp.com one. If sign-in or the map ever breaks after a change here, deleting the Content-Security-Policy entry restores the old behaviour.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://apis.google.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:; img-src 'self' data: blob: https:; connect-src 'self' https:; frame-src 'self' https://*.firebaseapp.com https://accounts.google.com; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self' https://tripai-app.web.app https://tripai-app.firebaseapp.com https://travel-ai-6de47.web.app https://travel-ai-6de47.firebaseapp.com
geolocation=(self), microphone=(self), camera=(), payment=(), usb=(), bluetooth=()

headers.comment: Hashed filenames, so the content behind a URL never changes.
Every route that serves the shell. Without the bare '/' and the extensionless patterns, Firebase applies its own max-age=3600 and a redeploy stays invisible for an hour.
The offline service worker: always revalidated, so a change to it reaches everyone on their next visit rather than up to an hour later.
